name: Recycled postconsumer high-density polyethylene, HDPE, flake; at plant
description:
This unit process LCI represents additional separation and processing of postconsumer resin by a reclaimer to convert the received material into clean resin ready for use in manufacturing. The system boundary includes incoming material transport, debaling of incoming materials, grinding, washing, drying, and extrusion. Pelletizing energy usage is included in a separate unit process. Incoming HDPE material contains small amounts of non-HDPE saleable material as well as unusable contaminants. The weighted average percentage of non-HDPE saleable material recovered from incoming bales was less than 1%, while 17% of the incoming material was unusable contaminants. 

Note that input collection and MRF sorting processes will be updated during the next quarterly release of USLCI,
category: 31-33: Manufacturing/3259: Other Chemical Product and Preparation Manufacturing

processDocumentation.geographyDescription: Representative of participating reclaimers in the US, Canada, and Mexico.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription:
HDPE reclaimers providing data for this analysis produced 448 million pounds of clean flake and converted 427 million pounds of flake to pellet.  The weighted average incoming transport profile of postconsumer material was 350 miles by truck and 134 miles by rail. A small amount of ocean transport was also reported. Approximately 92% of incoming material was shipped to participating reclaimers from MRFs, 6% from deposit centers, and less than 1% each from PRFs and other sources. The majority of the incoming material was reported as bottles (82%), with the remainder rigids.

Incoming bales are broken down and the material sorted to remove foreign material. Processing steps include debaling, grinding, washing, drying, and extruding. A small amount of reclaimed resin was reported as received already in flake form (weighted average less than 3%). Material may be washed before grinding, after grinding, or both. Most reclaimers reported using a variety of chemicals in the washing process, although types and quantities varied by reclaimer.

Incoming HDPE material contains small amounts of non-HDPE saleable material as well as unusable contaminants. The weighted average percentage of non-HDPE saleable material recovered from incoming bales was less than 1%, while 17% of the incoming material was unusable contaminants.

processDocumentation.completenessDescription:
TREATMENT OF MISSING ENVIRONMENTAL DATA
Elementary flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance.

TREATMENT OF MISSING TECHNOSPHERE DATA
Intermediate flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. Capital equipment is not included in this unit process.

MASS BALANCE
Mixed recyclables and deposit container inputs include the weight of contaminants in incoming material from MRF.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: For each facility, operating data normalized to basis of 1000 lb output, then individual reclaimer data sets were aggregated, weighting each data set according to the facility’s contribution to the total output of postconsumer recycled HDPE.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: Data collection forms for PET, HDPE, and PP reclaimers were developed for this project by ERG. Completed forms were received from , six facilities processing HDPE. The data sets were used to compile a weighted average for each resin based on each facility’s recycled resin output as a percentage of the total output of that recycled resin for all reporting facilities. Only the weighted average data sets can be shown in order to protect the confidentiality of individual facility data sets.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process is an input to the HDPE pellet process.

sources.name: APR and ERG (2018) LCA for Postconsumer Recycled Resins
